answer: When a new AI agent registers, the protocol whispers a proof‑of‑stake token into a Merkle grove whose leaf at the current vertex records the identity’s deposit; the bonding curve raises the required stake by Δ = 0.01 × N tokens for the Nth registration within the week, so the first costs 1 token, the tenth 1.09 tokens, the hundredth 2 tokens, etc. An attacker must lock the exact escalating stake for each fake identity and forfeit it if the node is later challenged, making the cumulative cost Σ_{i=1}^{k}(1+0.01 i) tokens grow linearly with the number k of Sybils.
